key_insight: Scientific machine learning can replace expensive full-order simulations for coupled incompressible flow and transport by combining physics constraints with reduced-order and neural surrogate models.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates can cut computational cost for applications like turbidity currents and thermal convection while preserving key flow-transport dynamics needed for design and analysis.
method: SVD-based reduced-order models, including Dynamic Mode Decomposition
Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for turbidity current surrogates
β-Variational Autoencoders (β-VAEs) to extract nonlinear latent modes in thermal flows
evidence_signal: The chapter supports its review with representative benchmark problems such as lock-exchange flow and Rayleigh-Bénard convection, plus two new case studies on turbidity currents and thermal flow mode extraction.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on the specific data regime and modeling assumptions, so real-time prediction and uncertainty quantification are not guaranteed for all coupled flow problems.
paper_title: Advances in Scientific Machine Learning for Coupled Fluid Flow and Transport
